newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-WE'VE DONE NOTHING YET, SAYS JOHNSON.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WE'VE DONE NOTHING YET, SAYS JOHNSON.

text.p: Victorious British Lions skipper Martin Johnson attempted to play down the significance of his side's gripping 25-16 victory over South Africa in Cape Town on Saturday.
"It's something you dream about -- winning a test in South Africa -- but what we will be saying pretty soon tonight to the lads is that it's no good winning one test if you lose two," said Johnson.
"We can't start celebrating when we have won nothing. We have got to come back with another win and then we can start enjoying ourselves."
The win in the first match between the sides in 17 years had an extra historical resonance as neither side has lost the first test in a series in South Africa and gone to win the rubber.
"Don't tell me that," said Lions coach Ian McGeechan who saw his bold selection of a heavily-outweighed front row vindicated.
"But every Lions test victory must be savoured whether it's the first, second or third in a series -- they are all special."

The Lions pack held their own although they were forced on the defensive for long periods and only came through in the final 10 minutes with match winning tries from scrum-half Matt Dawson and wing Alan Tait.
"This was probably the best victory I have ever played in," said winger Tait who has the distinction of being the first man to play rugby league and rugby union for the British Lions.
"The defence was awesome. I don't think they gave us the credit we deserved but today we have earned their respect and I'm sure they will come out twice as hard next week."

McGeechan added: "It's always nicer when you have got momentum on defence and, although they scored two good tries and there were passages in the game where we were on the back foot, we rode the storm and took our chances when they came."
Springbok coach Carel du Plessis put a brave face on the result: "The match was one of lost opportunities and chances.
"But I still have every confidence in this team. I believe in them and I believe they are the best combination to come back into the series."
Skipper Gary Teichmann said: "If we had played badly and hadn't been in the game then we might have been worried but that wasn't the case.
"What bothered me was that we spent long periods in their half but the points didn't come.
"We often got through the first tackle but the cover defence was very good.
"But the series is still open and we are looking forward to Durban. Confidence is still high in our squad. We will learn from our mistakes."
The second test is in Durban on Saturday with the third game in Johannesburg on July 15.
